definition: The parafovea is the area just outside the center of gaze, where visual information can still be taken in while attention is focused on a word at the point of fixation. In reading research, it refers to the region from which nearby words may be partly processed at the same time as the directly fixated word.

reasons: The packet supports parafovea as the region outside the fovea used in reading experiments, but it does not support the broader general description “the area just outside the center of gaze” or the claim about attention being focused on a word at fixation.

The packet supports parallel semantic processing of a parafoveal word and a foveal word, but it does not specifically support the phrasing that nearby words are “partly processed at the same time as the directly fixated word” as a general definition.
The definition is close to the packet’s reading-research context, but it overgeneralizes beyond what is explicitly supported by the source text.

The packet does not support the claim that the parafovea is “the area just outside the center of gaze.” It only operationalizes parafovea as a location where a simultaneously presented word (W2) is processed relative to a foveal word (W1).

The definition’s reading-specific phrasing (“nearby words may be partly processed at the same time”) is broadly consistent with the packet’s description that semantic information can be extracted from the parafovea in parallel with the fixated/foveal word, but the first sentence’s “just outside the center of gaze” element is unsupported.
